verdict.line: You lose this if you trade autos into his empowered Q heal at close range; you win it by poking with ranged Q before level 6 and bursting with Mega Gnar's W-R stun once you have it.

brief.thesis: Gnar is ranged and mobile in mini form while Yorick is purely melee until his Mist Walkers spawn, so the entire lane is about forcing trades at 1100-range Q distance instead of inside his Last Rites auto-attack range. The counter-pressure comes from his W (Dark Procession) wall, which can box you into melee range right as you'd rather be kiting — and from his 160-second R, which OP.GG's own data says to neutralize before committing to a fight.

theirWindow.when: Dark Procession wall boxes you in
theirWindow.what: If his W wall lands behind or beside you mid-trade, back off immediately rather than fighting — it turns a kiting lane into a forced melee exchange where his empowered Q sustain wins the extended trade.

yourWindow.when: His Q (Last Rites) is on cooldown
yourWindow.what: Last Rites is only 6-4s on cooldown but it's his only source of sustain and trade damage — when it's down, step up and land free Q (Boomerang Throw) pokes or an E (Hop) bounce off a minion since he has nothing to punish the auto-trade with.

start.why: The highest-winrate start (53.6% over 84 games) — the extra sustain and damage matter because you're trading autos at range but he can still close distance and punish with Last Rites.

boots.why: 88.9% pick, 50% winrate — flattens the repeated auto-attack chip from his Mist Walkers and his own autos when he does get in range.

core.why: The 63.6%-winrate path starts here; the move speed and burst proc help you catch him between Q poke and E bounce before he can wall himself off.
Shred stacks from your own autos let your Mega Gnar fights end faster, which matters since his R Maiden buffs his damage the longer a fight drags.
Best-performing third item in the data (63.6% over 11 games) — the shield absorbs the Mist Walker chip and his empowered Q burst in all-ins.

situational.when: he's building toward sustained walker swarms and kiting you down
fights are turning into prolonged auto-attack trades instead of clean burst windows
his Last Rites heal is outpacing your poke damage in lane

runes.keystoneWhy: 48.7% winrate, 28.5% pick — the move speed and sustain reward exactly the kite-and-poke pattern you want against a melee-only laner. Master-tier Gnar players instead run Lethal Tempo (across 1,803 games) — that fits players committing to sustained auto-attack trades in Mega Gnar form rather than pure poke-and-retreat.

summoners.why: Flash+Teleport is run in 62% of games at this matchup — Yorick's wall-and-split playstyle rewards being able to reset waves and reinforce other lanes. Flash+Ignite (65.5% winrate, 21.2% pick) is the stronger choice if you're confident taking the solo-kill advantage the data gives you.

playing.title: Poke with Q before level 6
playing.detail: Boomerang Throw hits from 1100 range with a slow; land it and back off rather than following up into his auto-attack range, since Last Rites turns any close trade into a heal for him.

playing.title: Watch his Q buff icon
playing.detail: Last Rites empowers his next attack with bonus damage and a heal — never walk into melee range while that buff is up on him.

playing.title: Bounce with E off minions
playing.detail: Hop lets you bounce off any unit you land on and travel further — use it on a minion to reposition and re-engage with Q rather than jumping directly onto Yorick.

playing.title: Don't fight inside his wall
playing.detail: Dark Procession blocks movement — if he drops it near you mid-trade, that's your cue to disengage, not commit, since it removes your kiting space.

playing.title: Time your Mega Gnar transformation
playing.detail: Save your rage-fueled transformation for a moment you can land Wallop's stun into R — Mega Gnar loses your ranged poke, so only flip when you can immediately convert it into a stun combo.

playing.title: Kill the Maiden before fighting
playing.detail: After he hits level 6 and summons it, his attacks against the Maiden's target deal bonus damage — focus the Maiden down first so his all-in loses that damage amp, exactly as OP.GG's own matchup note advises.

brief.patchCaveat: Build paths, runes, summoners, and all win-rate figures above are measured from live games on the current patch (16.20.1); the mechanical reasoning and trade-pattern advice are my own read of the kits.

stats.opponentTip: Focus early game on applying pressure to gain lane control. After reaching level 6, get rid of his (R) before fighting him.
